newsitem.title: USA: Indian Point nuke return seen easing NY line limit.
newsitem.headline: Indian Point nuke return seen easing NY line limit.

text.p: Return of the Indian Point nuclear unit 3 is expected to ease the transmission congestion that plagued the New York Power Pool (NYPP) over the past several weeks, the New York Power Authority (NYPA) said.
"It should be alleviated somewhat, but IP2 (Indian Point 2) is still out," said Ira Fine, a NYPA spokesman.

NYPA's 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 3 reached half power this morning after a month-long shutdown for various repairs. The adjoining 975 MW Indian Point 2, operated by Con Edison, is expected to restart by early next week after being shut January 27 to correct problems that made the feedwater valve inoperable.
Following those outages, interruptible or non-firm daily power deliveries across the so called "Central-East" interface in southern NYPP were often disrupted.

NYPA owns about half the high-voltage lines that run through Central-East. The interconnect is the gateway to bring cheap power from western New York to New England and New York City, where native generation comes from more expensive fuel oil or natural gas.
"We had to cut our interruptible contracts due partially to both nuclear units being down," Fine said. "There are not enough lines to bring down (non-firm) power to New York City."
Non-firm power is purchased with the understanding that delivery may be interrupted due to periods of high energy demand and/or transmission constraint to insure stable grid operation.
Transmission capacity at the Central-East point was further reduced by maintenance on several high-voltage lines.
"In the past week, we have cut our firm contracts," he added.
Fine noted transmission tightness at Central-East is a "chronic" problem because demand for transmission capacity far outweighs transmission availability.
